Subject: QBR: Competitive signals & pricing playbook (read-ahead)

Team —

Attached is a concise read-ahead for QBR prep that pulls together competitive pricing moves, three notable model releases, and initial impact estimates for our hosted and Dedicated funnels. High-level takeaways: 

- Pricing: Two mid-market providers (Competitor A, Competitor B) have announced limited-time subscription discounts (~15-25%) and a new usage cap tier that is driving fast trials.
- Model releases: Competitor C published an optimized LLM v2 claiming 20% latency improvement on 8k context and a smaller quantized variant targeted at inference-on-demand.
- Positioning: Messaging is shifting to "predictable low-cost inference" — they emphasize deterministic response times and marketplace billing.

Why this matters for QBR: these moves change our competitive narrative for mid-market churn risk and create a short-term push on price-sensitive trials. We should: 1) update the Competitive slide in the QBR deck, 2) add an OKR checkpoint for retention risk at the top of accounts list, and 3) propose a temporary promotional play for new trial signups (sales-led).

Please review the attached one-pager (qbr_competitive_signals_may2027.pdf) and the pricing tracker. I want a short ack and any edits by EOD Tuesday (May 3) so we can lock the deck.

Action asks:
- Markus: can you add a short note on SLA/credits exposure (2 slides max)?
- Laura: can you sanity-check the churn estimates in the tracker?
- Karthik: please surface any partner impact (marketplaces, AP partners).
- Marissa: coordinate a one-slide customer anecdote (if we have a field example).

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
VP, GTM Strategy | Redwood Inference

I dug into the tracker and ran a quick product impact estimate (attached). Additional context:

- Competitor C's LLM v2 appears to be optimized for shorter sequences; the 20% latency claim likely holds for 2–4k contexts but depends on batch behavior. Their quantized variant is compelling for high-volume inference on commodity GPUs.
- Competitor A's subscription tier includes an API token cap but waives overage for the first 90 days — that's a classic trial-to-paid lever.

Suggested slide changes:
1) Add a heatmap for accounts by exposure (top 30).
2) Add a technical note on model variant trade-offs (latency vs quality) so we can rebut in customer Q&A.
3) Propose a 6-week promotional pilot for sales to test retention impact (we should start gating by account size).

I've attached a short spreadsheet with rough revenue exposure buckets (prod_impact_estimate.xlsx).
